unit.title: Why we agree to be governed
unit.needIt: Rules you did not choose still protect you. Seeing what life is like with nobody in charge explains why people accept police, courts and taxes at all.
unit.why: Imagine a world where no one follows rules and everyone is out for themselves. People would live in constant fear because anyone could take what they have at any moment. To stop this, people agree to a 'social contract' where they trade some personal freedom for the safety of a community.
unit.outcome: Explain why a government is considered legitimate based on the idea of mutual benefit.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you follow traffic lights or wait in a line at a store. You do it because you trust that everyone else is following the same rules to keep things moving smoothly.
unit.do: Think about one rule you follow every day. Ask yourself if you follow it because you want to, or because you know everyone else does too.

quiz.q: What is the main reason Hobbes thinks we need a state?
quiz.why: Hobbes argues that the state is the only way to ensure a comfortable and safe life.
quiz.quote: Hobbes' answer is, having a civil state, having civil society, is the only effective means of what he calls commodious self-preservation.

quiz.q: What does Hobbes say about human equality?
choices: People are physically and mentally equal
quiz.why: He argues that because everyone has the same ability to kill or learn, they are roughly equal.
quiz.quote: They are physically equal, in the sense that each of them has the live possibility of killing and of being killed.

quiz.q: What is the 'state of nature' according to Hobbes?
choices: A war of all against all
quiz.why: Hobbes describes the state of nature as a condition of constant conflict and fear.
quiz.quote: The result will be a war, says Hobbes, of every man against every man, not necessarily a hot war in the sense of violence going on at every moment.

quiz.q: What happens to industry and culture in the state of nature?
quiz.why: Without safety, people cannot plan for the future or build things.
quiz.quote: In addition, there is no place for industry, because the fruit thereof is uncertain, and consequently there is no culture of the earth

quiz.q: What is a 'right of nature' for Hobbes?
quiz.why: It is the fundamental freedom to do whatever is needed to stay alive.
quiz.quote: Each human being has rights that Hobbes explicitly calls calls inalienable, to engage in whatever way he or she can to self-preservation.

quiz.q: What is the third law of nature?
quiz.why: The third law is the requirement to keep promises to ensure others do the same.
quiz.quote: The third law of nature, according to Hobbes, is that you need to perform your covenants. That is, you need to do what you have promised.

quiz.q: Why are covenants invalid without enforcement?
quiz.why: If you think someone else will break a promise, you have no reason to keep yours.
quiz.quote: Covenants, he says, are invalid if you fear that the other party may renege.

crystal.key: People agree to a social contract to escape a life of fear and gain security.

decoys.text: The state of nature is a historical fact.
decoys.why: Hobbes says the argument works regardless of whether the state of nature actually happened.

decoys.text: Justice is a natural human instinct.
decoys.why: Hobbes and Glaucon suggest justice is a social notion created by agreements to avoid suffering.

crystal.aha: Because we are naturally equal and self-interested, we must trade some freedom for a government that guarantees our safety.

scene.analogy: A four-way crossing with no lights

actors.label: You give up going first. You get home.

beats.say: Four roads meet. No lights, no signs.
Each fears the others, so nobody is safe.
Lights make everyone wait, and everyone gets through.
We give up some freedom to a common power and get peace.
